PhotoKit engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume photo-library capability covers storefront language. Xcode, privacy settings, and Connect actually separate picker behavior from product-page copy:

  • PHPickerViewController & limited library access — in-app code that presents the system Photos picker or requests limited photo access. Controls which assets users can attach. Does not generate Chinese listing text.
  • NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription — Info.plist string shown in the system permission sheet. Separate from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains photo-import value to buyers.
  • PhotoKit asset queries — engineering work when your app reads metadata or thumbnails beyond the picker sheet. Not App Store Connect listing fields.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of picker integration.

Working Photos picker flows in the binary and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other. AppLocale covers how you describe photo picking on the product page in zh-Hans, not how you implement PHPicker or PhotoKit.

  • Privacy nutrition labels (different) — data-collection disclosures when photo access touches analytics. See Privacy nutrition labels listing guide — not picker-sheet copy on utility apps.

Your screenshots may show multiple surfaces in one gallery. Listing copy should name the correct one per frame — a system Photos picker sheet is not a camera viewfinder, not an AR plane overlay, and not a Files document browser.

Photos-picker-specific listing copy — what translates differently

Library-picking listings use vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers evaluate photo-import claims — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Choose Photos vs Limited Access vs full library

Your listing should match the permission model your app actually uses — one-time picker selection, limited library access with ongoing subset, or full library when accurate — without promising access levels your binary does not request. AppLocale aligns storefront phrasing with your English claims and stated behavior; we do not invent photo permissions.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need photo-import search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 相册, 选图, and 从相册导入 each signal different intent from generic productivity keywords.

Screenshot captions on picker frames

Gallery frames that show the Photos picker sheet, limited-access UI, or album selection need one-line zh-Hans captions — "从相册选择照片" not "Choose Photos" burned into the product page story.

Common mistakes on Photos-picker-themed zh-Hans listings

  • Assuming picker integration localizes automatically — PHPicker shipped in the binary; zh-Hans row never added or left blank
  • Only translating the description — subtitle, keywords, and Choose Photos screenshot caption lines still English
  • Conflating library picking with camera capture — listing says 拍照 or "take photos" when the app only imports from the library
  • English Limited Access on zh-Hans screenshots — Connect caption fields are Chinese but burned-in picker labels on PNG exports are still Latin
  • Expecting AppLocale to implement PHPicker — picker configuration and authorization flows are engineering tasks outside listing rewrite scope
  • Mixing ARKit or Files vocabulary into picker copy — AR session overlays and document-browser UI belong on different listing guides, not Choose Photos frames
  • What's New still English after picker launch — see What's New in Simplified Chinese when limited-library support shipped in a recent version
